idiom_name: EF Core implicit join entity with skip navigations
implementation_notes: EF Core (5 and later) maps the many-to-many by convention: two collection navigations on the two entity types are enough and EF creates the join entity and the join table itself, named by convention (Post + Tag gives PostTag) with a composite primary key over the two foreign keys and cascade deletes. The skip navigations let application code add a Tag to a Post directly - EF inserts or deletes the link row - which is exactly Association Table Mapping with the link table kept out of the model. Choose the implicit form while the association has no payload; the moment it needs one, the explicit join entity below takes over.
pitfalls: The join entity has no configured .NET class by default and is represented as Dictionary<string, object> internally; do not depend on that representation, and configure an explicit join entity as soon as code must read the link rows.
Both sides are navigable, so adding the same pair from both navigations without a composite key (or a unique index) is the duplicate-link trap EF Core warns about for skip navigations.
Loading both collections eagerly produces a cartesian explosion; use filtered includes or split queries for graph reads.

variants.name: EF Core explicit join entity (payload and direct access)
variants.implementation_notes: When the link table carries data or must be queried directly, the join entity becomes a real class: PostTag with the two foreign keys plus its own columns, configured through UsingEntity<PostTag>(...) so both skip navigations stay available on the ends. This is the documented promotion of the pattern to an association entity - the table is now a first-class entity, and the many-to-many is expressed as two one-to-many relationships that happen to share a composite key. It costs a class and a manual link creation step, and buys payload columns, direct queries and audit fields on the association itself.
pitfalls: With an explicit join entity the link must be created explicitly (new PostTag{...} plus SaveChanges): the skip navigation still works for the ends but the payload has to be filled in by hand.

Adding the join entity to the model without using UsingEntity can make EF model it as a plain entity, silently producing two one-to-many relationships instead of the intended many-to-many behaviour on the ends.
Composite key values are immutable: changing one side of a link means deleting the row and adding a new one.
